page.overview:
Who is Danny O'Bannion?

Danny O'Bannion is a fictional character created by Keith Herber for the first edition of Arkham Unveiled, published by Chaosium in 1990 for the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, where he is presented as the owner of Lucky Clover Cartage Company, a front for O'Bannion's bootlegging operations. O'Bannion's name is Herber's homage to the American screenwriter and director Dan O'Bannon (who co-wrote the screenplay of Dark Star (1974) and wrote the screenplay of Alien (1979) among other films), according to correspondence between Herber and fellow Call of Cthulhu writer Richard Watts during the development of Arkham Unveiled. Most recently, O'Bannion reappears in Chaosium's Arkham (2023), the first of several releases planned for the 'Arkham Unveiled' line (formerly known as 'Lovecraft Country') for the 7th edition of the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

O'Bannion has also appeared in publications from Fantasy Flight Games (establised 1995) for their Arkham Horror Files series of Cthulhu Mythos-related releases. Although primarily appearing in the now-discontinued Call of Cthulhu Living Card Game, he has also been referenced in other media, such as Peter J. Evans' franchise tie-in novel Feeders from Within.

Danny O'Bannion is a major player in the shady underworld of 1928 Arkham, heading the organised crime coalition dubbed The Syndicate, a powerful group with an interest in every illegal activity in town. Conducting much of his business from the Clover Club, a shady den of iniquity, his group is at constant war with the Sheldon gang, bootleggers plying their trade in opposition to the Syndicate.

O'Bannion has a daughter, a beautiful young woman named Naomi, who also works for the Syndicate.
